skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - explain why it's important to communicate technical concepts in non-technical language - explain the types of communication that can be used with internal and external stakeholders, and their impact
You can: - undertake data profiling and source system analysis - present clear insights to colleagues to support the end use of the data

You can: - use official data classification when authoring documents - apply internal procedures, policies and technologies to ensure secure data handling - identify and address ethical considerations when working with data - address data compliance issues using internal processes
You can: - implement simple data solutions such as data pipelines, following established approaches and standards - create repeatable, reliable and reusable data solutions

You can: - develop a basic understanding of an unfamiliar or emerging technology, or a familiar technology in a new data context, with guidance - share what you learn with colleagues, including how it could help deliver more value from data
You can: - design simple data exchange or integration solutions using established patterns or modelling techniques - include security features in your data integration designs

You can: - explain the concepts and principles of data modelling - produce, maintain and update relevant data models for an organisation’s specific needs - reverse-engineer data models from a live system

You can: - use metadata repositories to complete complex tasks such as data and systems integration impact analysis - maintain a metadata repository to ensure information remains accurate and up to date

You can: - investigate problems in systems, processes and services, with an understanding of the level of a problem, for example, strategic, tactical or operational - contribute to the implementation of remedies and preventative measures

skill: Programming and build (data and analytics engineering)
expected_level_description: You can: - design, code, test and deploy programs or scripts following standards and good practice - write readable, maintainable code - use automation to improve the software development life cycle - consider and adopt appropriate security measures in your solutions

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - read and use FHIR resources, profiles, and APIs - build or test simple integrations under guidance - check messages against a specification
You can: - explain the difference between a clinical terminology and a classification - recognise common terminologies such as SNOMED CT and ICD
You can: - work with pseudonymised data and apply disclosure checks before releasing outputs - recognise when linked or detailed data could identify a patient
You can: - explain how health IT systems can harm patients, for example through wrong, missing, or delayed information - report a possible clinical safety issue through the right route
